find:
'**Understand.** Read the text until you know exactly what it means.',
  '**Plan.** Ask who will read your translation and why.',
replace:
'**Plan.** Ask who will read your translation and why.',
  '**Understand.** Read the text until you know exactly what it means.',
reason: Chapter 2 (both its structure and its worked example) puts Plan before Understand, so the four steps in Start here should be in the same order.

find: Imagine a friend who reads only Arabic asks what an English sign says. You would not read out the words one by one; you would say what the sign **means**, in good Arabic. That is translation.
replace: Remember the sign in the park (Start here): you did not read out the words one by one; you said what the sign **means**, in good Arabic. That is translation.
reason: This repeats the Start here park scenario almost word for word; referring back to it avoids the repetition and keeps the guided flow.

find: Translation has been described as “saying almost the same thing” (Eco, 2003).
replace: Umberto Eco called translation “saying almost the same thing”, the title of one of his books (Eco, 2003).
reason: The quoted phrase is the (translated) title of Eco’s Italian book in the References, so it should be presented as a title rather than as a quotation from an English text.

find: And your translation has one test: your reader must understand it.
replace: And your translation must pass a basic test: your reader must understand it.
reason: Saying understanding is the only test contradicts the faithfulness and accuracy required in Chapter 2; it is a necessary test, not the only one.

find: '**Sight translation**: reading a written text aloud in another language.',
replace: '**Sight translation**: reading a text written in one language and saying it aloud in another.',
reason: As written, a beginner may think the text is already in the other language; the new wording makes the change of language explicit.

find: Freelance and in-house translators both do commissioned work,
replace: Freelance translators (who work for many clients) and in-house translators (who work for one employer) both do commissioned work,
reason: ‘Freelance’ and ‘in-house’ are used without explanation in a book for complete beginners.

find: 'Commissioned translators follow the brief; self-initiated translators choose their own texts.'
replace: 'Commissioned translators follow the client’s instructions; self-initiated translators choose their own texts.'
reason: The term ‘brief’ is only introduced in Chapter 2; Chapter 1’s body speaks of ‘their instructions’.

find: '**Be faithful** ({{الأمانة}}): do not add or remove meaning. Aim to be faithful, accurate and acceptable to the reader.',
replace: '**Be faithful** ({{الأمانة}}): do not add or remove meaning. Aim to be accurate and acceptable to the reader as well.',
reason: ‘Be faithful … Aim to be faithful’ repeats the same word in consecutive sentences.

find: _She takes her pills on time_ → {{تتناول دواءها في موعده}}
replace: _She had lunch_ → {{تناولت الغداء}}
reason: The example meant to show the meanings of _have_ contains the verb _takes_, not _have_, so it does not illustrate the point.

find: 'Do not translate _is_, _am_ or _are_ with {{يكون}}:
replace: 'Do not translate a simple _is_, _am_ or _are_ with {{يكون}}:
reason: {{يكون}} is correct in many present contexts (habitual truths, after {{أن}}, future), so the absolute ban is inaccurate; ‘a simple’ limits it to the case shown.

find: never translate _is_ with {{يكون}}
replace: do not translate a simple _is_ with {{يكون}}
reason: The summary repeats the over-absolute ban on {{يكون}}; it should match the corrected body text.

find: {{أنتم}} (men or a mixed group) or {{أنتنّ}} (women)
replace: {{أنتم}} (three or more men, or a mixed group) or {{أنتنّ}} (three or more women)
reason: Since {{أنتما}} covers two people, a beginner needs to know that {{أنتم}} and {{أنتنّ}} are for three or more.

find: Some short English words must not be translated with their first dictionary meaning:
replace: Some common English words must not be translated with their first dictionary meaning:
reason: _Eventually_ and phrases such as _to see the Roman ruins_ are not ‘short words’, so ‘common’ describes the list accurately.

find: '**Modern Standard Arabic**: the Arabic of newspapers,
replace: '**Modern Standard Arabic** ({{الفصحى المعاصرة}}): the Arabic of newspapers,
reason: The other two bullets give the Arabic term; MSA should too, using the term already given in the chapter’s key terms.

find: Most problems fall into four groups:
replace: Most translation problems between English and Arabic fall into four groups:
reason: ‘Most problems’ is vague for a beginner; the sentence should say which problems are meant.

find: ['{{حضر الطلابُ المحاضرة.}}',
replace: ['{{حضر الطلابُ المحاضرة.}} (When the verb comes first, it stays singular: {{حضر}}, not {{حضروا}}.)',
reason: The key agreement change (plural verb becomes singular in verb-first order) is never explained, so a beginner cannot see why the answer is {{حضر}}.

find: '**AR → EN**: start with the subject, split long sentences, keep one of two synonyms, add “is”.'
replace: '**AR → EN**: start with the subject, split long sentences, turn a pair of synonyms into one expression, add “is”.'
reason: The body renders {{شجاعٌ مِغوار}} as _very brave_ (an intensified single idea), not by keeping one of the two words.

find: Translate what the speaker means, in a way that sounds natural in the target language.
replace: Translate so that your reader understands what the speaker means. If the indirect sentence works the same way in the target language, keep it indirect.
reason: As written, beginners may turn an indirect remark into an explicit request (e.g. ‘Please close the window’), which changes the text; the translator should convey the intended meaning, usually by keeping the indirectness where it works.

find: 'Translate what the speaker means, not only what the sentence says.'
replace: 'Make sure your reader understands what the speaker means, not only what the sentence says.'
reason: The summary must match the corrected Step 2, so it does not tell beginners to replace indirect speech with an explicit version.

find: Use a familiar measure: _about 20 centimetres_.
replace: Use a familiar measure: _about 23 centimetres_.
reason: A span is conventionally nine inches (about 22–23 cm), so ‘about 20 centimetres’ is inaccurate (settles the writers’ note).

find: A word can mean several things (Chapter 5).
replace: Chapter 5 showed that meaning has layers. Many words also have several meanings.
reason: Chapter 5 deals with denotation, connotation and speaker meaning, not with words that have several meanings, so the reference points to the wrong content.

find: (a container, such as a phone case)
replace: (a container, such as a glasses case)
reason: A phone case is {{غطاء}} or {{جراب}} in Arabic, not {{علبة}}; a glasses case is naturally {{علبة النظارة}}.

find: The course materials define collocation as “the company a word keeps”.
replace: It has been defined as “the company a word keeps” (Translation Team, n.d.).
reason: ‘The course materials’ are unknown to readers of the handbook; citing them as (Translation Team, n.d.), as Chapters 1, 21 and 22 do, points to the References entry (settles the writers’ note).

find:
['Translate: _heavy rain_', 'Translate: _a close friend_', 'Translate: {{اتّخذ قراراً}}'],
        ['{{مطر غزير}} (not {{مطر ثقيل}}).', '{{صديق مقرّب}}.', '_He made a decision._']],
replace:
['Translate: _heavy rain_', 'Translate: _deliver a lecture_', 'Translate: {{عقد مؤتمراً صحفياً}}'],
        ['{{مطر غزير}} (not {{مطر ثقيل}}).', '{{يلقي محاضرة}} (like _deliver a speech_).', '_He held a press conference._']],
reason: Two of the three questions repeat items from the lists word for word, so they test memory rather than the skill; the new ones apply the same patterns to new partners.

find: Its words are frozen: you cannot change their order or replace one of them.
replace: Its words are frozen: you usually cannot change their order or replace one of them.
reason: Many idioms allow some variation (_a real piece of cake_; Baker, 2018, speaks of little or no variation), so ‘usually’ is more accurate.

find: ['p', 'Try them in this order (Baker, 2018):'],
replace: ['p', 'Here are five common ways (Baker, 2018). As a rule, try them in this order, but let the context decide:'],
reason: Baker describes these strategies but does not prescribe a fixed order; the order is the handbook’s own advice and should not be attributed to her.

find: 'An idiom with the same meaning and the same form, if one exists.',
replace: 'An idiom with the same meaning and the same form, if one exists: _to play with fire_ → {{يلعب بالنار}}.',
reason: The first strategy is the only one without an example, and beginners need to see that such matches exist.

find: '_to pull one’s socks up_ → {{شمّر عن ساعديه}}',
replace: '_to roll up one’s sleeves_ → {{شمّر عن ساعديه}}',
reason: {{شمّر عن ساعديه}} means ‘get ready to work hard’, which matches _roll up one’s sleeves_, whereas _pull one’s socks up_ means ‘improve one’s effort or behaviour’ (settles the writers’ note).

find: '_Boys will be boys._ → {{الولد ولد ولو صار قاضي بلد}}',
replace: '_Boys will be boys._ → {{الولد ولد ولو صار قاضي بلد}} (a colloquial proverb)',
reason: The proverb is colloquial ({{قاضي}} for MSA {{قاضيَ}}); Chapter 3 tells readers to use MSA, so it should be labelled (settles the writers’ note).

find: ولا بدَّ للتَّرجُمانِ من أن يكونَ
reason: The al-Jāḥiẓ quotation is cited as (al-Jāḥiẓ, 1965) without volume and page; please check it against the printed Hārūn edition (Vol. 1) and add the page.

find: (Translation Team, n.d.), or “rendering
reason: A definition from the team’s own unpublished course notes is introduced as what ‘experts’ say; please confirm the wording against the manuscript, or consider ‘Our course materials describe translation as…’.

find: as in a poem’s rhyme (Nida & Taber, 1969)
reason: The Nida and Taber principle is paraphrased without a page number (usually cited as p. 4); please check the printed edition, and note that the rhyme example is the handbook’s addition.
